hypothesis: In parse_receipt, when body.image is provided via Base64, the string is split and decoded via base64.b64decode without checking if len(image_bytes) > MAX_IMAGE_SIZE. An attacker can send an unbounded 50MB-100MB base64 payload that decodes directly into memory, bypassing the 20MB limit enforced on remote URLs and inducing an immediate OOM in a 512MB container.

convert_heic_to_jpeg and Pillow image operations execute synchronously inside an async def FastAPI route handler. Under high concurrency, CPU-intensive image decompression and re-encoding freeze the asyncio event loop for 100-300ms per request, starving concurrent SSE streams and health check probes.

When converting images to JPEG format using Pillow without alpha composite handling, passing RGBA or LA transparent images will trigger 'OSError: cannot write mode RGBA as JPEG', causing an unhandled 500 error instead of a sanitized response.

Cloud Run deployment specifies --memory 512Mi on 1 vCPU with default concurrency of 80. Decompressing 48MP smartphone photos generates 140MB+ uncompressed raw bitmap per request. 3-4 concurrent receipt parsing requests exceed the 512Mi container ceiling, triggering SIGKILL (OOMKilled 137) and cascading container restarts.

worker.js checks pathname.startsWith('/api/parse-receipt') to bypass to Vercel origin, but the frontend actually calls /api/ai/parse-receipt. This creates an unmaintained dead-code path and architectural confusion regarding which tier is responsible for receipt processing.
